t:
In this Act:
    (1) Congressional intelligence committees.—The term “congressional intelligence committees” means—
        (A) the Select Committee on Intelligence of the Senate; and 
        (B) the Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence of the House of Representatives.  
    (2) Intelligence community.—The term “intelligence community” has the meaning given that term in section 3(4) of the National Security Act of 1947 (50 U.S.C. 401a(4)).

fable.w: This section only defines the terms "congressional intelligence committees" and "intelligence community" for use in the Act. The tempting reading is that mentioning committees implies consultation, but congressional committees are inside the federal government. No process is created for anyone outside the federal government to be consulted on, comment on, or challenge a federal decision.

opus.w: This is a definitions section. It only defines 'congressional intelligence committees' and 'intelligence community' and creates no process for anyone to take part in a federal decision. The committees mentioned belong to Congress, which is inside the federal government, so even interaction with them would not count as participation.
opus.b:
1. **Reasoning.** It might look relevant because the section names "congressional intelligence committees," and committees can suggest advisory panels or oversight. That reading fails because these are committees of Congress, which is inside the federal government. The section only defines terms. It sets up no process involving anyone outside the government.

2. **Label.**

qwen_chat.w: This section only provides definitions for terms used in the Act. It does not establish any process for consultation, coordination, or input from parties outside the federal government. Both Congress and the intelligence community are considered inside the federal government for the purposes of this definition.
qwen_chat.s: In this Act: (1) Congressional intelligence committees.—The term “congressional intelligence committees” means— (A) the Select Committee on Intelligence of the Senate; and (B) the Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence of the House of Representatives. (2) Intelligence community.—The term “intelligence community” has the meaning given that term in section 3(4) of the National Security Act of 1947 (50 U.S.C. 401a(4)).
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might think that defining "intelligence community" or "congressional intelligence committees" implies some form of interaction or participation, but these are merely definitions of terms for the purpose of the statute. There is no requirement for consultation, coordination, or input from outside parties in this specific text. The entities defined (Congress and federal intelligence agencies) are inside the federal government.
